fatal_errors: The proposed method is bulk experimental testing of as-cast material rather than molecular-dynamics tensile simulation of a single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn model.
It omits the crystallographic-orientation, temperature, and strain-rate matrix central to the target problem.

It changes the scientific comparison from deformation behavior within FeNiCrMn to a comparison against CoCrFeMnNi, so it cannot reconstruct the target conclusions about anisotropy, thermal softening, or strain-rate response.
The proposed comparison does not isolate the effect of Co removal because alloy composition, processing history, grain structure, and phase state may all differ.
The cited evidence provides only general background on HEAs and the Cantor alloy; it does not support the predicted mechanical consequences of removing Co from FeNiCrMn.
explanation: The response recognizes that FeNiCrMn mechanical properties can be investigated by uniaxial loading and microstructural characterization, but it misses nearly all defining elements of the target method. The target uses atomistic simulation to vary crystal orientation, temperature, and very high strain rate and then applies DXA/CNA to identify vacancy-assisted Shockley-partial nucleation and stacking faults. The generated hypothesis instead focuses on an as-cast polycrystalline comparison with the Cantor alloy and offers an uncertain Co-removal mechanism. Its experiment could test that separate hypothesis to some extent, but matched processing and stronger compositional controls would be required, and the supplied citations do not validate its mechanistic prediction.
